title: Pseudo-coherent reconstruction over a surjective locally nilpotent ring tower
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(A_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse sequence of commutative unital rings, with surjective unital transitions $u_n:A_{n+1}\to A_n$ such that every element of $\ker u_n$ is nilpotent. Put $A=\varprojlim_n A_n$, the ring of compatible tuples with componentwise operations. For each $n$, let $K_n\in D(A_n)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], meaning isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $A_n$-modules. Suppose maps $t_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n$ in $D(A_{n+1})$ (the target by restriction of scalars) have scalar-extension adjuncts $K_{n+1}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n$. Derived scalar extension and its adjunction to exact scalar restriction are those of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], specialized to ordinary modules on the one-object point site. Regard the tower in $D(A)$ by restriction of scalars. If $(K,p,\delta)$ is any derived limit of this tower [def-weil-derived-limit], with projections $p_n:K\to K_n$, then $K$ is pseudo-coherent and, for every $n$, the scalar-extension adjunct of $p_n$ is an isomorphism $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n$ in $D(A_n)$. There is no Noetherian hypothesis, no required adic presentation of the tower, and no common nilpotence exponent; pseudo-coherence is assumed at every level.

source.place: Tag 0CQF, lemma-Rlim-pseudo-coherent-gives-pseudo-coherent, branch where every K_n is pseudo-coherent; projection-induced reduction maps and arbitrary derived limits as in its proof and Remark 0H9J (derived.tex, remark-functoriality-derived-limit).

proof.text: Choose a bounded-above finite-free representative $P_1^\bullet$ of $K_1$ and a marking $\beta_1:Q(P_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}K_1$, using the definition of pseudo-coherence. Fix $b$ with $P_1^i=0$ for $i>b$. Put $J_n=\ker(u_n)$. For $x\in J_n$, choose $r$ with $x^r=0$; then $(1+x)\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}(-x)^j=1$. Thus every element of $1+J_n$ is invertible. The quotient $A_{n+1}/J_n$ identifies with $A_n$: the map $[a]\mapsto u_n(a)$ is injective by the definition of the kernel and surjective by hypothesis. This explicit identification will be used in each lifting application.

Inductively, suppose $(P_n,\beta_n)$ has been chosen with cutoff $b$. Write $\gamma_n:K_{n+1}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n$ for the adjunct specified in the hypothesis. Apply the marked lifting lemma with $R=A_{n+1}$, $I=J_n$, $F=P_n$, $K=K_{n+1}$ and $\alpha=\beta_n^{-1}\gamma_n$. Its hypotheses hold: $K_{n+1}$ is pseudo-coherent by assumption, and step 1 checked the unit condition. It gives $(P_{n+1},\beta_{n+1},\theta_n)$, with the same cutoff, and
$$\beta_n Q(\theta_n)c_{P_{n+1}}=\gamma_n(\beta_{n+1}\otimes^{\mathbf L}A_n).$$
Define $v_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$ by $x\mapsto\theta_n(x\otimes1)$. The coefficient adjunction, normalized on K-flat representatives, identifies the adjunct of $Q(v_n)$ with $Q(\theta_n)c_{P_{n+1}}$. Bounded-above free complexes are K-flat. Consequently the displayed equality is equivalent by the adjunction bijection to $\beta_n Q(v_n)=t_n\beta_{n+1}$. The models therefore represent the actual transition maps, including their markings.

Choose a finite basis of each $P_1^i$, with index set of size $r_i$, empty for $i>b$. Given a basis of $P_n^i$, lift its vectors through $v_n^i$ to $P_{n+1}^i$. This is possible since $u_n$ is surjective and $\theta_n^i$ is an isomorphism. They define $f:A_{n+1}^{r_i}\to P_{n+1}^i$, whose reduction is the chosen basis isomorphism. Finite Nakayama makes $f$ surjective. The target is free, hence projective, so lift its identity through $f$ to split $f$. Its kernel $T$ is a direct summand of $A_{n+1}^{r_i}$, generated by the projections of the $r_i$ standard vectors. Reduction of this direct sum decomposition gives $T/J_nT=0$, since the reduction of $f$ is an isomorphism. Apply the same finite Nakayama statement to $0\to T$ to get $T=0$. Thus the lifted vectors are a basis. Induction gives compatible bases in every degree. In these bases $v_n^i$ is coordinatewise $u_n$. A compatible sequence in $P_n^i$ is therefore exactly $r_i$ compatible sequences in $A_n$, giving $P^i:=\varprojlim_nP_n^i\cong A^{r_i}$. Componentwise differentials define a complex $P$; they square to zero in every coordinate. It is zero above $b$. The scalar map $P\otimes_A A_n\to P_n$, $x\otimes a\mapsto a x_n$, sends these bases to these bases, hence is a chain isomorphism.

Every $v_n^i$ is surjective, as checked in step 3. The surjective-module-complex tower-limit theorem gives a Roos triangle for $Q(P)$ with first arrow whose components are $Q(P\to P_n)$. The isomorphisms $\beta_n$ from step 2 form an isomorphism of towers after restriction to $A$. Their product therefore intertwines the two $1-s$ arrows. Rotate the Roos triangles of $Q(P)$ and of the specified $(K,p,\delta)$ so that these arrows are first. Axiom TR3 completes the commuting square of product isomorphisms to a morphism of triangles; rotate back to obtain $h:Q(P)\to K$ with $p_nh=\beta_n Q(P\to P_n)$ for all $n$. The levelwise-isomorphism theorem for Roos-triangle completions makes $h$ an isomorphism. This applies to the specified derived limit and its projections, without assuming a canonical derived-limit functor.

Step 3 exhibited $P$ as bounded above and termwise finite free, and step 4 gave $Q(P)\cong K$. This is precisely pseudo-coherence of $K$. Tensoring with a free module is a sum of copies and preserves exact sequences, so $P$ is termwise flat. The bounded-above flat-complex theorem makes $P$ K-flat. Derived change of rings thus computes $Q(P)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_n$ by the ordinary tensor complex $P\otimes_A A_n$.

Let $\rho_n:K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_n\to K_n$ be the adjunct of the given projection $p_n$. By naturality of the coefficient adjunction, $\rho_n\circ(h\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_n)$ is the adjunct of $p_nh$. By the projection equality from step 4 and the adjunction's chain-level normalization, this adjunct is $\beta_n\circ Q(a_n)\circ c_P$, where $a_n:P\otimes_A A_n\to P_n$ is $x\otimes a\mapsto ax_n$. Step 3 proved $a_n$ is a chain isomorphism. Each of $\beta_n$, $Q(a_n)$, $c_P$ and $h\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_n$ is invertible, so $\rho_n$ is invertible. This proves the assertion for the scalar-extension adjunct of each specified projection.

tool_uses.why: Generic normalized coefficient adjunction identifies the actual transition and projection adjuncts on free models; the unit has no replacement for it.
Generic bounded-flat K-flatness computes scalar extensions on the free models; no unit-specific result replaces it.
Finite Nakayama lifts compatible bases and kills the finite split kernel, without nilpotence of the entire ideal.
Generic degreewise-surjective module tower theorem gives the Roos triangle with the actual projections.
Generic triangulated comparison makes a Roos-triangle completion invertible; it transfers the model to the specified derived limit.
